### load packages
```{r}
library(vcfR)
library(adegenet)
library(StAMPP)
library(ggplot2)
library(SNPfiltR)
```

### Filter vcf file to remove technical replicates and invariant SNPs
```{r, eval=FALSE}
#read vcf
v<-read.vcfR("~/Desktop/2026.eagle.mountain/bwa.FLSJ.filtered.miss90.mac3.vcf.gz")

#remove the technical replicate with the lower sequencing depth
vcfR.trim<-v[,colnames(v@gt) != "Aph_woodhouseii_B-303"]

#remove invariant SNPs
vcfR.trim<-min_mac(vcfR.trim, min.mac = 1)

#write out the filtered/trimmed vcf 
vcfR::write.vcf(vcfR.trim, file="~/Desktop/2026.eagle.mountain/final.trimmed.snps.vcf.gz")

#how many SNPs and missing percentage in this final filtered vcf?
vcfR.trim
table(extract.gt(vcfR.trim), useNA = "always")
#23 samples, 9419028 SNPs, 2.44% missing genotypes

#thin to no SNPs closer than 5KB
filt.thin<-distance_thin(vcfR.trim, min.distance = 5000)

#how many SNPs and missing percentage in this final filtered vcf?
filt.thin
table(extract.gt(filt.thin), useNA = "always")

#write out the filtered/trimmed vcf 
vcfR::write.vcf(filt.thin, file="~/Desktop/2026.eagle.mountain/final.trimmed.snps.5KBthinned.vcf.gz")

#calculate stats on this vcf
x<-missing_by_sample(vcfR.trim)
x[["unfiltered.stats"]]
```

### perform splitstree analysis 
```{r, eval=FALSE}
#convert vcfR to genlight
gen<-vcfR2genlight(vcfR.trim)
#check sample names (remember the splitstree gui won't let you visualize more than 10 characters in a sample name, and all sample names must be unique)
gen@ind.names
#edit your sample names to fit this criteria
gen@ind.names<-gsub("Aph_californica_","cal", gen@ind.names)
gen@ind.names<-gsub("Aph_woodhouseii_","woo", gen@ind.names)
#double check sample names
gen@ind.names

#assign sample names as populations (population assignments are a requirement for the stampp functions, but can be arbitrary here because we want a pairwise divergence matrix among all samples, not samples assigned populations)
pop(gen)<-gen@ind.names
#make pairwise divergence matrix among all samples
sample.div <- stamppNeisD(gen, pop = FALSE)

#export for splitstree
stamppPhylip(distance.mat=sample.div, file="~/Desktop/2026.eagle.mountain/final.filtered.splits.txt")
```


### check out the results
```{r}
#open this file using the splitstree GUI. Export the network as a .svg file and use the knitr function 'include_graphics' to show the resulting tree:
knitr::include_graphics("~/Desktop/2026.eagle.mountain/final.filtered.splits.svg")
#further changes made in adobe illustrator to prepare this for publication
```
